chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Ibn Riʾāb, from Muḥammad ibn Qays, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

Umm Salamah, the wife of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله, had a bondwoman, and she stole from some people. She was brought to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله, and Umm Salamah spoke to him concerning her. Then the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله said: “O Umm Salamah, this is one of the limits set by Allah; it is not to be neglected.” So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله amputated her hand.

key_terms.حَدٌّ: a prescribed legal punishment fixed by sacred law
key_terms.حُدُودِ اللَّهِ: the divinely established legal limits and ordinances
key_terms.فَقَطَعَهَا: he carried out the amputation punishment upon her
key_terms.لَا يُضَيَّعُ: it is not to be neglected or left unenforced
key_terms.مَوْلَاةٌ: a female bondwoman or freedwoman under the care or affiliation of another

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith teach about enforcing the hadd for theft without favoritism?
ai.summary: This hadith relates an incident in which the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله enforced the hadd punishment for theft despite the intercession of Umm Salamah. It underscores the principle that Allah’s legal limits are not to be set aside due to personal ties or status.
